_note: English text for the engine-test kingdom map (roadmap 1.8, D-110): interface labels and the invented names of the Fenn March. Keys are ids; {braces} are filled by the ui.
ui.title: The Fenn March
ui.subtitle: as kept by The Lantern Company
ui.mapLabel: Inked map of the Fenn March. Drag or use the arrow keys to move, plus and minus to zoom.
phone.mapLabel: Inked map of the Fenn March. Pinch to zoom, drag to move, tap a place for its details.
phone.places: Places and parties on the map
phone.letter.far.title: The party has reached {place}
phone.letter.far.body: Marrow writes that the road was kept and the lantern is lit. The clock has stopped for you; press Play when you are ready to send the party home.
phone.letter.home.title: The party is home
phone.letter.home.body: Marrow and the company are back at the hall with mud to their knees. The clock has stopped; press Play to send them out again.
phone.kindline.town: A walled market town of the Fenn March.
phone.kindline.village: A small village on the March roads.
phone.kindline.landmark: A place the old maps mark with a ring.
phone.kindline.threat: Something is wrong here, and the guild is watching.
phone.kindline.guild: A guild house with its banner flying.
phone.kindline.party: A party of the guild, on the road.
phone.more.town.0: The first lamp on the map hangs over its door.
phone.more.landmark.0: Shepherds will not graze their flocks within a mile of it.
phone.more.threat.0: The road is closed; carters go round by the fen paths.
phone.more.guild.0: Our own company. Its lantern hangs over the hall door.
phone.more.guild.1: A hard-nosed rival that takes the paying contracts first.
phone.more.guild.2: A free company of sellswords with a long ledger.
phone.more.party.0: Walking the road out and back, a few days at a time.
phone.about.town.0: Home to the guild hall, a drying loft and far too many ravens.
phone.about.town.1: Known for its ford, its fair and its argumentative ferrymen.
phone.about.town.2: The reeve holds court here under a crooked oak.
phone.about.town.3: Lake town where the eel-smokers outnumber the guards.
phone.about.town.4: A hill town with a good wall and a bad temper.
phone.about.town.5: The harbour, loud with gulls and salt-wardens.
phone.about.town.6: Fen-edge town built on piles; the cellars are always damp.
phone.about.town.7: A mining town under the Stone Spine; the bells ring for every shift.
phone.about.village.0: Sheep, a mill and one very old well.
phone.about.village.1: A mere with a rumour in it.
phone.about.village.2: A weir where the fishers mend their nets.
phone.about.village.3: Peat cutters and a tavern with no sign.
phone.about.village.4: A crossroads hamlet famous for its pies.
phone.about.village.5: Withies are cut here for baskets and hurdles.
phone.about.village.6: Low barns and a lower mood after the floods.
phone.about.village.7: Carters meet here to swap news and wheels.
phone.about.village.8: Salt pans along the shore, white in the sun.
phone.about.village.9: A landing stage where the fen boats tie up.
phone.about.village.10: The gate of the wood, with owls on the gatepost.
phone.about.village.11: A small quay for small boats.
phone.about.village.12: A weaving village; every roof has a loom under it.
phone.about.village.13: Candle makers boil tallow here in the reeds.
phone.about.village.15: Willows lean over the village street.
phone.about.village.16: Nettle beds and a stubborn priest.
phone.about.village.17: Thatchers live here and say so.
